key_insight: The U-statistic structure of GRPO policy gradients turns group-size selection from trial and error into a variance-ratio estimation problem.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive group sizes can reduce policy-gradient estimation error and improve reasoning-model training with modest additional computational cost.
method: Express GRPO group-size selection through U-statistics and variance-ratio estimation.
Use a pessimistic ratio estimator that accounts for denominator uncertainty.
Apply a jackknife-based selection rule and analyze three sample-size regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower policy-gradient mean squared error and improved policy optimization versus fixed-group-size baselines on synthetic Reasoning Gym tasks and real-world math and code benchmarks.
watch_item: Small variance-ratio denominators make estimation unstable; implementation must account for denominator uncertainty rather than rely on naive plug-in estimates.
